settings.name_in_paper: Online preference learning model (alpha-informative feedback, linear utility)
unmapped: Coactive feedback: user returns an improved object bar y_t rather than a reward or a pairwise comparison outcome
Feedback quality defined by alpha-informativeness with per-round slack xi_t >= 0: U(x,bar y)-U(x,y) = alpha(U(x,y*)-U(x,y)) - xi_t
Utility U(x,y) = w*^T phi(x,y) with joint feature map ||phi(x,y)|| <= R; cardinal utilities never observed
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the learning algorithm receives a context $\bx_t \in {\cal X}$ and presents a (possibly structured) object $\by_t \in {\cal Y}$. In response, the user returns an object $\bby_t \in {\cal Y}$ which the algorithm receives as feedback. ... We say that user feedback is {\em $\alpha$-informative}, if for some $\alpha \in (0,1]$ and $\xi_t \ge 0$ ... U(\bx,\by) = \bw^{*\top} \phi(\bx,\by) ... such that $\|\phi(\bx,\by)\| \le R$

symbols.alpha_inf: informativeness parameter alpha in (0,1] of the user feedback
symbols.L_feat: bound R on the joint feature norm ||phi(x,y)||
symbols.S: ||w*||, norm of the unknown utility parameter

conditions: feedback is alpha-informative with slacks xi_t >= 0
utility is linear: U(x,y) = w*^T phi(x,y) with ||phi(x,y)|| <= R

source.label: thm:bound
source.quote: Under $\alpha$-informative feedback the algorithm in Figure \ref{perceptron} has regret \text{REGRET}_T \le \frac{1}{\alpha T} \! \sum_{t=1}^T \xi_t + \frac{2R \|\bw^* \|}{ \alpha \sqrt{T}}.

results.notes: Paper's REGRET_T is the average regret (divided by T); multiplied by T here. The bound is deterministic (holds for every sequence), recorded as realized_regret/almost_sure. Mapping of coactive feedback to 'dueling' is approximate. Algorithm requires an argmax oracle over Y.
